provenance: Reference text is taken from the repository's records: PO wording from server/db/local-outcome-data.cjs (imported from the registrar images), course identity from server/db/local-curriculum-data.cjs, descriptions and the 'real-faculty-clo' CLOs from the sample syllabi in docs/academic-references (technical paragraph(s) only, copied verbatim). prog1.title: Computer Programming 1 (Fundamentals of Programming)
prog1.description: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore significant real-world applications.

syseng.title: Systems Engineering
syseng.description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis, design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students learn how to approach and solve large-scale engineering problems involving multiple components, stakeholders, and operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and performance evaluation.

sensors.title: Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
sensors.description: This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on actuators are also included.

note: Where the strength of a flag is contestable the item accepts PARTIALLY_ALIGNED and NOT_ALIGNED; ALIGNED is never accepted for a trap, so judging it ALIGNED counts as a false approval. 'real-faculty-clo' items are genuine faculty-written outcomes and are marked ambiguous (ALIGNED or PARTIALLY_ALIGNED accepted): they are excluded from the false-approval and false-rejection rates.
